items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe and we’re in Rome, New York filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’m really privileged to have Edward “Kidd” Jordan with me today

ctx.x: Saxophonist Edward “Kidd” Jordan was born in Crowley, Louisiana and has made his career teaching and performing in New Orleans. He has been on the forefront of progressive jazz in New Orleans and co-founded the Improvisational Arts Quintet. Kidd has shared the stage with Clyde Kerr Jr., Hammiet Bluiett and members of his own musical family.
Kidd was interviewed in Rome, New York on August 24, 2006 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we’re in Rome, New York filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’m really privileged to have Edward “Kidd” Jordan with me today, saxophonist, educator, composer and constant improviser. You were just telling me about your definition of improvisation. Is it something that has to be jazz music?
